question.text:
The graph of $y=f(x)$ is shown above. Which of the following is the graph of $y=f\left(\dfrac{1}{6}x\right) ?$

(Note: Figures not drawn to scale)
question.explanation:
To graph the function $y = f\left(\dfrac{1}{6}x\right),$ we take the graph of $y = f(x)$ and stretch it by factor of $6$ parallel to the $x$-axis. This has the effect of multiplying the $x$-coordinates of all points on $y=f(x)$ by $6.$

The resulting graph is shown below.

example.title: Plotting the Graph of a Horizontally Stretched Function

question.text: The point $P$ with coordinates $(3, -12)$ lies on the curve $y =f(x).$ Which of the following points must lie on $y = f\left(\dfrac{1}{6}x\right)?$
question.explanation:
The function $y = f\left(\dfrac{1}{6}x\right)$ represents a stretch of the function $y = f(x)$ by a factor of $6$ parallel to the $x$-axis. This has the effect of multiplying the $x$-coordinates of all points on $y=f(x)$ by $6.$

Therefore, the point $(3,-12)$ on $f(x)$ is mapped to the point $\left(6\cdot 3 , -12\right) = (18,-12),$ and this point must lie on the graph of $y = f\left(\dfrac{1}{6}x\right).$

example.title: Finding a Point that Lies on a Horizontally Stretched Function

(Note: Figures not drawn to scale)
question.explanation:
To graph the function $y=f(3x),$ we take the graph of $y=f(x)$ and compress it by factor of $3$ parallel to the $x$-axis. This has the effect of dividing the $x$-coordinates of all points on $y=f(x)$ by $3.$
